subject: Post-call: Model evals & multilingual fit - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Müller <elena.mueller@globex.de>, Akira Sato <akira.sato@tokyo-retail.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps - multilingual evals

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - great conversation and clear signal that Globex Retail cares about consistent UX across EU and APAC locales. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: validate model fit for customer-facing product search & merch copy generation across German, French, Spanish (EU) and Japanese, Korean (APAC).
- Immediate asks from your side: share a 1-2k sample of anonymized queries and expected outputs per locale (Elena: you mentioned a sample export).
- Our proposed plan: run a small-scale eval (accuracy / hallucination / tone) on 3 candidate model configs, plus a locale-specific prompt set we drafted.

Attachments & links: I uploaded our prompt sets and baseline eval plan here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-multilingual-evals ("redwood_multilingual_prompt_set_v1.csv").

Next steps / owners: 
- Globex: share sample exports (Elena) - ideally anonymized query+expected output per locale by EOD Thu.
- Redwood: we (Neha + Rishi) will run the eval matrix against: 1) xlarge-multilingual-v2 (full float), 2) opt-1.3b-quant (int8), 3) gptj-6b-qlora (tuned) and provide a short benchmark (latency, cost/token, quality metrics) within 72 hours after we have samples.
- Discuss data residency / GDPR constraints - we can run EU-region canary if needed.

If that sounds good, I'll queue the evals once we have the sample.

- Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Elena Müller <elena.mueller@globex.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 11:05:23 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - multilingual evals

Thanks Marissa - that plan sounds good. I'm attaching a small sample export for DE/FR (anonymized) so you can start. A couple quick Qs before you run anything: 

1) Can you confirm the recommended models and any expected latency for a 256-token generation in eu-west-1? We have strict SLA expectations for search suggestions.
2) GDPR/data residency: would the evals run on EU-hosted infra by default or do we need to request a VPC/private deployment?

Attachment: globex_data_sample_de_fr.zip

Elena Müller
Head of International Product - Globex Retail
elena.mueller@globex.de

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Müller <elena.mueller@globex.de>, Akira Sato <akira.sato@tokyo-retail.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - multilingual evals

Thanks Elena - received the sample. Quick answers inline: 

1) Recommended candidate models (we'll run all three in the matrix):
   - xlarge-multilingual-v2 (best quality; ~120-160ms/token on dedicated A100-class infra; expect 200-300ms p50 for 256-token generation in EU-region Hosted)
   - opt-1.3b-quant (good latency/cost tradeoff; quantized int8; expect 60-100ms/token p50)
   - gptj-6b-qlora (middle ground; tuned for retail prompts; watch for occasional style drift)

2) GDPR / residency: we can run the evals in eu-west-1 Hosted (no private deployment required) - if you need audit-proof isolation we can run on a Dedicated EU tenant or Private VPC; let us know.

I've kicked off the eval plan template and linked the benchmark doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/multilingual-2027. Neha / Rishi will pick this up once they have the file system access to the sample.

Proposed timeline: 48-72 hours after Rishi has the sample and confirms access.

- Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: prioritization & quality regression checks (Globex eval)

Team - quick internal note to prioritize DE and JA first for this eval (highest risk for user-visible regressions). Key asks for the eval harness: 
- Baseline: run current production model (opt-1.3b-quant) vs xlarge-multilingual-v2 vs gptj-6b-qlora; generate 3 outputs per prompt; measure hallucination rate, entity accuracy, tone match, and token/time cost.
- Locale checks: German (formal tone, compounding nouns), French (politeness markers), Japanese (honorifics/keigo) - include native speaker reviewers where possible.
- Regression alert: set threshold for entity-level F1 drop >5% as a red flag.

I'll attach the short plan: eval-plan-20270604.md (contains the rubric + upload steps). Can you confirm infra (eu-west-1 worker pool vs apac worker pool) and ETA?

- Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 10:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: prioritization & quality regression checks (Globex eval)

On it - I'll pull the sample into the eval harness today. Plan: spawn eu-west-1 workers for DE/FR/ES and ap-northeast-1 for JA/KR test runs to capture region-specific latency. Expected runtime: 48-72 hours after start.

Quick request: can Globex provide any locale-specific prompt translations (EN->JA/DE) or should we use our translation pipeline? If they want to review translations, ask them to attach a CSV with original+localized prompts.

- Rishi

From: Akira Sato <akira.sato@tokyo-retail.jp>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Elena Müller <elena.mueller@globex.de>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 15:22:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps - multilingual evals

Thanks team - sounds good. Two quick items from procurement/ops side: 

1) Pilot timeline: can we get a short pilot (EU + APAC canary) within 2 weeks? We need numbers to justify the budget.
2) Data privacy: for the pilot, would the sample data be processed in a Redwood-managed EU worker pool or would it need to be VPC? We prefer EU-hosted only for production; pilot can run in managed EU infra if you provide a data deletion certificate after the run.

If you can confirm the pilot window and deletion proof, procurement will prioritize this.

Akira Sato
Director, Engineering - Tokyo Retail Group
akira.sato@tokyo-retail.jp
